source_snapshot.procedure: For one existing user ID, run `user set name`, `user set password` and `user priv <ID> <Privilege level> <Channel number>`, then check the user list.
source_snapshot.criteria: The account is modified successfully and displayed correctly.
source_snapshot.script: Internal `modify-user-account-ipmi` path whose exact revision is unavailable here.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL changes only username and privilege, omits the required password operation and privilege channel, exposes the management password with `-P`, hard-codes cipher suite 17, and uses a generic list as proof without old/new authentication or authorization behavior.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly requires a disposable account, one-property-at-a-time changes, complete channel baseline, protected secrets, old/new authentication, bounded authorization, independent recovery and cleanup.

old_problem: The safe property matrix, protected credential method, explicit channel, property-specific behavioral oracles and deterministic rollback were not bound, while DeepSeek omitted password coverage entirely. This kept a fully defined standard IPMI workflow in Pending even though all missing values are Project runtime parameters rather than an unresolved engineering command.
disposition_reason: Retain the source name, password and channel-privilege operations as three independent cycles on one approved disposable account. Each cycle captures baseline, applies exactly one change, verifies inventory plus effective behavior, restores the exact baseline and verifies the inverse before the next cycle. Account values, explicit channel, privilege and session policy are Project bindings. This preserves coverage, prevents cross-property attribution and eliminates the need for an additional engineering decision.
decision_basis: XLSX row 942, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 943 were directly reviewed; the next identity was verified as Functionality row 943 / variant 476fd2ff967ff903.

The source consistently names three standard IPMI modifications. Missing user ID, old/new values and channel are executable runtime parameters under the approved parameterization rule, not undefined core semantics.

Pinned upstream ipmitool source defines the name, protected prompted password and explicit-channel privilege commands, enforces a 16-byte username limit, maps standard privilege values and defaults an omitted privilege channel to current channel. The source's channel placeholder must therefore be supplied explicitly.

A user list can show name and per-channel privilege but cannot prove a password, authentication transition or effective authorization. Old/new login and bounded allowed/denied checks are required in the relevant cycle.
ED-03/ED-13 and ED-33 through ED-38 permit the parameterized standard contract while requiring source coverage, explicit confirmation, recovery, no unsafe substitution and engineer-owned verdict.

test_case.test_name: Modify and restore one disposable IPMI account's name, password and explicit-channel privilege in isolated cycles
test_case.purpose: Verify through the original IPMI path that one approved disposable account can independently change username, password and privilege on one explicit management channel, that each new value is displayed or behaviorally enforced, and that each property returns to its exact approved baseline without changing protected identities or other channel/SOL state.
required_package: Target BMC/firmware identity, pinned supported ipmitool version, protected RMCP+ recovery credential path and approved cipher policy
Existing disposable numeric user ID, complete old name/enable/access/SOL/session state across all relevant channels and protected-account exclusion list
Unique old/new usernames within target 16-byte/encoding policy and approved collision/reserved-name rules
Known old/new test-user secrets satisfying target 16/20-byte policy, supplied only by protected prompt/provider and never recorded
Explicit target channel, baseline/new standard privilege values, vendor/Project privilege mapping and bounded allowed/denied read-only action matrix
Project policy for existing sessions after name/password/privilege changes, independent recovery session and exact per-property restore plan
Three separate point-of-action approvals or one signed plan explicitly enumerating each change/restore pair and stop conditions
test_case.test_command: CRITICAL ACCOUNT WRITE. Preserve logs and capture complete per-channel user/access/SOL/session baseline from an independent recovery administrator. Prove the immutable ID is disposable and the new name is unique. Cycle 1 NAME: after approval run `ipmitool ... user set name <ID> <NEW_NAME>` once, verify explicit-channel list/name, old-name denial and new-name protected bounded login; restore `<OLD_NAME>` once and prove the inverse. Cycle 2 PASSWORD: run `ipmitool ... user set password <ID>` with protected double prompt and no password argument, prove OLD_SECRET denial and NEW_SECRET success without logging either; restore OLD_SECRET through the same prompt and prove NEW_SECRET denial/OLD_SECRET success. Cycle 3 PRIVILEGE: run `ipmitool ... user priv <ID> <NEW_PRIV> <CHANNEL>` with the channel explicitly supplied, verify `user list <CHANNEL>`, `channel getaccess <CHANNEL> <ID>` and approved allowed/denied actions; restore `<OLD_PRIV>` on the same channel and repeat the inverse. After every write compare all other channels, access flags, SOL, protected users and sessions. Stop before the next cycle on any mismatch. Do not use `-P`, an implicit channel, the unreviewed script or WebUI/API substitution.
test_case.expected_result: Name cycle shows only the approved name transition, old-name denial/new-name login, then exact old-name restoration with reverse authentication. Password cycle shows only old-secret denial/new-secret login, then exact old-secret restoration with reverse authentication; no secret appears in evidence. Privilege cycle shows the approved new standard privilege only on the explicit channel, correct bounded allowed/denied behavior, then exact old-privilege restoration. Every cycle leaves unrelated name, password behavior, enable/access/SOL/session and protected accounts unchanged, and final state equals the complete baseline.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires all three independent cycles, each with explicit approval, one change, authoritative readback or behavior, exact restore and reverse proof, followed by full baseline equality. A generic list or successful exit cannot prove password or authorization; omitting password/channel coverage, batching properties, exposing a secret, changing another channel/account, failing old/new behavior, or incomplete restoration is FAIL and stops. Missing account values/channel/role/session policy is NOT READY, not Engineering Decision Pending.
safety_gate: Never modify a root, fixed, production, owner, recovery or unknown account. Correlate the immutable numeric slot and all relevant channels before every cycle.

Use an independent recovery administrator and protected new/old test-user credential prompts/providers. Never place any password in `-P`, arguments, history, process listings, logs, screenshots or records.
Change only one property at a time and restore it fully before the next. Execute each write once, read back immediately and do not automatically retry or proceed after an unexpected state.
Supply `<Channel number>` explicitly for privilege. Do not assume current channel, grant Administrator for convenience or translate nonstandard vendor role labels without authoritative mapping.

Preserve security/audit logs; do not clear evidence. Stop on wrong ID/channel, collision, secret exposure, excess privilege, unexpected session behavior, protected-account delta or recovery impairment.
Do not execute the internal script until its exact revision is inspected and proven to retain the three isolated cycles, protected secrets, explicit channel and rollback.
expected_evidence: Target/BMC/ipmitool identity, approvals, disposable/protected ID classification and complete redacted per-channel/access/SOL/session baseline
Name-cycle write/audit/list plus old/new login results, exact restore and reverse proof
Password-cycle redacted write/audit plus old/new secret behavior, exact restore and reverse proof with no secret material
Privilege-cycle explicit channel/old-new values, list/getaccess and bounded allowed/denied results, exact restore and reverse proof
Per-cycle other-channel/protected-account no-change comparisons, final baseline equality, preserved logs and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: At the first failed checkpoint, stop all later cycles and preserve evidence. From the already-open independent recovery session, restore only the current property from its approved baseline: old name, old secret through protected prompt, or old privilege on the exact channel. Re-read every relevant channel/access/SOL/session state and protected identities. If the wrong/protected account changed or the baseline secret is unavailable, do not guess or bulk-edit; invoke the approved vendor account-recovery procedure and rotate exposed test secrets.
